text: The police do not have to charge you. They charge your car.
provenance: The police can take your car, your cash, even your house — and never charge you with a crime

text: Civil asset forfeiture works on a legal fiction. The case is not brought against the person. It is brought against the thing.
provenance: Civil asset forfeiture works on a legal fiction that sounds almost absurd when you first hear it. The case is not brought against the person. It is brought against the thing

text: That is why these cases have such strange names. The government versus a car. Versus a house. The property itself is treated as the suspect.
provenance: That is why forfeiture cases have such peculiar names — the government versus a car, versus a sum of cash, versus a house. In the eyes of the law, the property itself is treated as the suspect.

text: And because the case targets the object, the protections you expect in a criminal trial do not all apply. In many places the owner never has to be convicted.
provenance: And because the case targets the object, not the owner, the protections you would expect in a criminal trial do not all apply. In many places, the owner does not have to be convicted of a crime to lose the property.

text: Ask yourself how a person keeps the presumption of innocence when the case is not filed against a person at all.
